item.content:encoded:
I told myself that I wouldn't post on the wiki while away, but I couldn't help but to write something here. Firstly, I'd like to apologize to my team for dropping out, despite the unlikely circumstances that forced me to. Y'all have done amazing amazing work with a GoI that I didn't particularly like prior to this contest and I'm fairly sure that not getting to be a part of it is my biggest regret as far as my site activity goes. Secondly, a huge congratulations to the Serpent's Hand team. I haven't had time to read barely any of your work, but from what I've seen all I can say is that you completely deserve it. To the other teams, you've made a lasting contribution to the site that has around the board inspired me personally and will continue to be an inspiration to members, old and new alike, for a very long time. Lastly, I'd like to personally thank TroyL for conceptualizing and organizing a contest. Everything from the tinyest rules, to the timeframe, to the judges was done exceptionally. Thank you.

I can say with complete certantity that this is the single best thing that has happened to the site since I joined.

item.title: Some Comments from the Judges on the Different Teams:
item.content:encoded:
Some of the judges sent along comments (and some are still planning to), but I wanted to go ahead and share some things from the lists of commentary I've received already.

Fifthists:

  • "The guidelines are very loose and all over the place, but that makes sense for the Fifth Church and the sky is really the limit in terms of originality."
  • "This is easily one of my favorite GoI entries. They took something I was completely indifferent to and made me love it, the bastards."
  • "Skillfully executed, and I never say things like that lightly."

CotBG:

  • "I like the ideas they brought to the table…[Their object format is] basically a kind of Tale, so inherently open-ended."
  • "Very differnt from what I'm used to, but it feels like its breathed some life into a GoI no one is writing about anymore."

MCF:

  • "I wussed out after the chapter the dog showed up in because I can't handle animal mutilation, but the execution of everything I saw up to that was flawless."
  • "Much more clever than I was expecting. I thought this would be boring (because I hate hate hate this GoI), and it ended up being better that I could have anticipated."

Herman Fuller:

  • "I hate clowns, but now, I want to love hating clowns. ;-;"
  • The new format was "surprisingly accessible."
  • "I really would have liked to see them go in more directions. It feels like the jumped on the circus bandwagon and just rode it hard. I get that it's a circus, but I wanted more circus of the disquiet. When they were doing that, I was enraptured."

UIU:

  • "It was like reading a spy novel with radioactive dogs."
  • "You had me at radioactive dogs, man."
  • "Really clever. There was some nice characterization there that I wasn't really expecting. Extremely pleased with this, overall."

AWCY:

  • "They've basically saved AWCY? as a GOI."
  • "I went from "Ehhhh…" to "DO WANT" on this GoI in the time it took for me to read this team's material. Your upvote is the drill that will pierce the heavens."
  • "I've always, always, always hated this GoI. And I still have to give them top points. This was amazing."

ORIA:

  • "I wish Bihj was around to see this. I think it would have made him extremely happy."
  • "The work put into making this original, interesting, and all around… just… damned good… is impressive. I was not expecting to be impressed by the ORIA."

CI:

  • "There are a lot of problems with the characterization in places, but the stories were fun. I smiled while I was reading them, and there's not much else I can say to sell them better."
  • "Not my Chaos Insurgency, but certainly one I could see existing. Felt darker than other iterations, which isn't a bad thing. Reminded me of some of the old CI objects we lost in the Mass Edit."

SH:

  • "The entries have been more fun to read than any other team's so far."
  • "Dear lord. Is THIS the stuff they're doing over at the Wanderer's Library? I want to get in on that…"
  • "Better than I was expecting. Much better. Loads better. This is one of those GoIs I sort of picture the hipsters imagining themselves as members of, and they've made it more. Instead of a World Of Darkness crossover conglomeration of nonsense and emotasticness, they've given life to something that I considered stillborn. Well done."

MC&D:

  • "I love them for making what they made, and I hope people write dozens of articles for it."
  • "One of the most interesting, fun, and unique takes on something that has started to feel old hat for me (but I'm an old fart around here anyhow). Excellent, overall. Just excellent."

item.title: FINAL RESULTS
item.content:encoded:
All teams were judged on a set of criteria related to: the quality of the work (usually determined by upvotes), the quantity of works written, the inclusion of the GoI, the originality of their tales and objects (or their take on those things), the New Object Format that was created for the contest, sportsmanship, and their 'gut reaction' to the over work as a whole. All told, each judge could award up to twenty-four points total to a team.

Judge Name 5th CotBG MCF HFCotD UIU AWCY? ORIA CI SH MC&D
Cream Soda 19 21 22 18 18 23 18 15 24 19
Fanta 17 17 18 14 16 15 20 12 20 13
Mountain Dew 17 13 18 12 18 14 17 17 19 11
Surge 7 22 4 7 13 18 4 7 7 15
"I.J.D.T." 14 12 17 12 9 16 15 6 19 16
RC Cola 18 16 20 14 18 20 16 9 23 14
Coke 14 15 19 14 21 11 16 17 23 18
Canada Dry 19 17 21 17 17 21 15 14 21 16
Pepsi Max 18 18 20 17 20 19 19 17 22 17
Finals 143 151 159 125 150 157 140 114 178 139
Average 15.9 16.8 17.7 13.9 16.7 17.4 15.6 12.7 19.8 15.4

Due to the plagiarism issue with the ORIA, all points awarded for originality were instead not awarded. MC&D is in a similar boat, as it was realized that they were missing a requirement for an 'original' object. All points for 'quantity' that were awarded were instead not awarded. Both these things were done in lieu of disqualification. I'm very sorry it shook out like this, guys. If you'd like to know your scores before those point changes, please let me know.

This means that our winners, in order, are:

The Serpent's Hand in first place!

Manna Charitable Foundation in second place!

Are We Cool Yet? in third place!

Congratulations, all of you! Excellent job!

item.title: ANNOUNCEMENTS!
item.content:encoded:
Firstly, everyone give yourselves a huge pat on the back. You'll all done some extraordinary work, and I'm proud of everyone, regardless of circumstances. I have some awesome announcements and some not-so-awesome announcements.

Disqualifications:

Firstly, two teams did not post any entries:

Team Name: Judo Kickstand, Kungfu Chopper: Cyclists of the Apocalypse
Team Name: The Commies

These two teams have been disqualified, and those in the teams will receive no participation prizes.

Secondly, the following teams have been disqualified for the following reasons:

Team Reason
Total Newbs Failure to meet minimum number of entries/participants.
FederationOfMisconception Failure to meet minimum number of entries.
Non Sequitur Failure to meet minimum number of entries.
The Other Game In Town Did not post entries by the deadline.
The Team That May Or May Not Be Called FRAF Failure to meet minimum number of entries/participants.

However, due to the work that people on these teams put in, all members of these teams who posted content will still receive participation prizes. Great work, guys, all of you who put forth the effort to get together things, especially those of you who were fighting against a strong current.

These disqualified teams will be left on the page, and their HUBs will continue to be linked to (until such a time as they are deleted, by site vote, if necessary).

Judging:

Judging will be starting soon. The judges are known only by pseudonym, though their final impressions of the ten, remaining teams will be posted for all to see, as well as the final math (and their comments) being visible. All judges may, if they wish, reveal who they are after the judging period has ended (in five days).

Some Statistics:

Not including hub pages, the contest has produced:

  • 124 Separate Pages
  • 115 Pages With Positive Ratings

This is more content than the Canon Contest (Or NYC2013), Time Contest, Five Questions Contest, and Under-Appreciated Contest combined.

I'd like to further point out that you all have changed the future of the site in a way. You've invented new things which people can adapt, run with, and delight in playing with. You've added to canons and built new perspectives on the ways things operate. You've taken the Groups of Interest — a highly neglected part of the site — and you've breathed new life into it.

I can not fully express to all of you how very, very proud I am of the work you've done. Excellent job, all.
